title: What an appraisal is
body: An appraisal is an unbiased, supported opinion of value as of a specific date, made by a licensed or certified appraiser following USPAP. Lenders order appraisals to protect their collateral.
example: A Reno buyer's lender orders an appraisal before approving the loan.
hook: Appraisal: an opinion, as of a date, for a purpose.

title: Market value and who may appraise
body: Market value is the most probable price in a fair, open sale. Federal law (FIRREA) requires licensed or certified appraisers for appraisals in many federally related loans. A real estate license alone doesn't qualify someone to appraise.
example: A Henderson listing agent prepares a CMA but doesn't call it an appraisal.
hook: Licensed to sell isn't licensed to appraise.

title: Principles that drive value
body: Highest and best use is the legal, possible, feasible use with the greatest value. Substitution says buyers won't pay more than for an equal alternative. Contribution says an improvement is worth what it adds, not what it cost.
example: A $60,000 pool in a Las Vegas neighborhood where pools add $25,000 contributes $25,000.
hook: Worth what it adds, not what it cost.

title: Three kinds of depreciation
body: Physical deterioration is wear and tear. Functional obsolescence is outdated design. External obsolescence comes from outside the property, like a new freeway, and the owner can't cure it.
example: A Reno home backs onto a newly widened highway. That's external obsolescence.

title: Comparing sales
body: The sales comparison approach adjusts recent sales of similar homes to match the subject. It's the main approach for single-family homes. Pick comps that are recent, nearby, and similar.
example: A Summerlin appraiser uses three sales within half a mile from the last 90 days.

title: Adjust the comp, never the subject
body: If a comp is better than the subject, subtract the value of the difference from the comp's price. If it's worse, add. The subject never gets adjusted.
example: A comp has a pool worth $20,000 and the subject doesn't. Subtract $20,000 from the comp's price.
hook: Comp better, subtract. Comp worse, add.

title: The cost approach
body: Value equals land value plus the cost to build the improvements new, minus depreciation. It works best for new buildings and special-use properties like schools or churches that rarely sell.
example: An appraiser values a new Carson City fire station with the cost approach.
hook: Land plus building new, minus wear.

title: Reproduction vs. replacement
body: Reproduction cost builds an exact replica, using the same materials. Replacement cost builds the same usefulness, using modern materials. Historic buildings usually call for reproduction cost.
example: Rebuilding a historic Virginia City storefront exactly as it was is reproduction cost.
hook: Reproduction is a replica. Replacement is the equivalent.

title: Income approach with a cap rate
body: Value = net operating income ÷ cap rate. NOI is effective gross income minus operating expenses. Mortgage payments are never an operating expense.
example: A Henderson fourplex nets $48,000 a year. At a 6% cap rate, it's worth $800,000.

title: Gross rent multipliers
body: For small rentals, value is roughly monthly rent times a gross rent multiplier from comparable sales. For larger properties, annual income times a gross income multiplier.
example: Similar Las Vegas rentals sell at a GRM of 160. A home renting for $2,000 suggests a $320,000 value.

title: CMA: the licensee's tool
body: A CMA compares recent sales, active listings, and expired listings to help a seller price or a buyer offer. Sold prices show what buyers paid. Expireds show what didn't sell.
example: A Reno agent's CMA shows sold comps around $510,000 and several expireds above $560,000.
hook: Solds show value. Expireds show too high.

title: CMA and BPO are not appraisals
body: A CMA or broker price opinion is a licensee's estimate. It isn't an appraisal and can't be called one. Lenders typically need an appraisal from a licensed or certified appraiser.
example: A Las Vegas lender asks a broker for a BPO on a foreclosure, then orders a full appraisal for the new loan.
hook: Never call a CMA an appraisal.
